title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "You don't get to rename the trophy, gang. You only get to give it back."
tagline: Week 10 — The Recap That Comes With A Warning Label (And A Name Change)
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Gather round, gang, and somebody get the smelling salts, because False Hope just scored 190.58. That's the highest score anybody has posted all season, 12.6 better than the old record, and they dropped it on Cracked Out Uncle to end a six-game win streak. Christian McCaffrey scored 46.3 by himself. George Pickens went from 0.0 last week to 43.5 this week, which is the kind of turnaround I usually only see in a halftime locker room with the lights off. The Steelers D/ST scored MINUS 7.0, the worst defense of the season. And the team formerly known as Champ 🏆 walked into the office, peeled the trophy off the door, and renamed itself 1 season wonder. Then lost a fifth straight with 16.1 points on the bench. Questionable or Kicked and the Lambs are tied at 7-3, four teams are tied at 4-6, and there's one team sitting alone in the basement holding last year's banner. Film's loaded. Let's roll.

matchups.recap: The cult has been raided. False Hope put up 190.58, the season high, and won by 47.12, the biggest margin of the week. Christian McCaffrey scored 46.3 on a 21.76 projection, the top starter in the league, and came within 0.82 of beating the Uncle's margin of defeat all by himself. Trevor Lawrence added 26.78, the Vikings D/ST 21.0 on a 4.96 projection, Blake Corum 20.9, DJ Moore 19.4 and Jordyn Tyson 19.0. Christian Watson (6.7) and Tucker Kraft (2.9) were the only soft spots, and the bench scored 0.0 because there was nothing left to bench. Cracked Out Uncle scored 143.46, which beats most teams most weeks. Chuba Hubbard went for 34.2 and Jayden Daniels 20.76, but Sam LaPorta gave 2.6 at TE and Jaylen Warren 9.1. Rashee Rice scored 13.2 on the bench, a 4.1-point swing over Warren that wouldn't have touched a 47-point hole. Six straight wins, over.
matchups.trashTalk: False Hope, ten weeks of me telling you the name was a warning, and you go and score 190. Fine. I'll eat it. Cracked Out Uncle, the streak is dead, and you've now allowed 1,428.04 points this season, the most in the league. You don't have a defense. You have a welcome mat.

matchups.recap: Patrick Mahomes, projected for 18.55, scored 35.42, and the Dingos won by an even 45.0. Chase Brown added 28.3 on a 13.53 projection, Amon-Ra St. Brown 25.8, Bhayshul Tuten bounced back to 20.3 and the Rams D/ST scored 16.0. Jordan Mason scored 5.9 on the bench, but he couldn't beat anybody he was eligible to replace. Perfect lineup. Somebody frame it. Kelce's Wildest Dream Team got 44.2 from Jahmyr Gibbs, a week after he gave 13.4, and 27.2 from Cam Skattebo on an 11.52 projection. Then Drake Maye scored 3.02 on a 21.97 projection, the biggest bust in the league, and DeMario Douglas gave 1.4. Josh Downs scored 15.3 on the bench (+13.9 over Douglas) and Omarion Hampton 17.5 (+11.3 over Rachaad White). That's 25.2 points left in the folding chairs. They'd still have lost by 19.8, but that's no excuse.
matchups.trashTalk: Kelce's Wildest Dream Team, your running back scored 44 and your quarterback scored 3. That's not a dream team, that's a group project where one kid did everything. Done Dingos, everybody wrote you off. You set a perfect lineup and won by 45. Turns out the dingo was just napping in the shade.

matchups.recap: The Lambs are tied for first. Emmett Johnson scored 35.1 on an 18.3 projection, Ja'Marr Chase 34.1, Tony Pollard 23.9, Jared Goff 20.42 and Derrick Henry 19.0. And then, gang, Omar Cooper Jr. started at FLEX and scored 0.0. Again. Same guy who gave 0.0 in Week 8 and cost them that game. This time Rhamondre Stevenson only had 1.5 on the bench, so it was a +1.5 swing and they got away with it. Major Tuddy had Parker Washington at 28.2, James Cook III 21.7, C.J. Stroud 20.44, CeeDee Lamb 20.2 and Cam Little kicking 19.0. Brock Bowers gave 3.8 on a 15.41 projection, and then the Steelers D/ST scored MINUS 7.0 on a 5.46 projection. That's a 12.46-point shortfall in a 12.48-point loss. Even if the defense had just hit its projection, Tuddy still loses by 0.02. Germie Bernard's 1.0 was the whole bench, the lineup was perfect, and they lost to a team that started a zero. That's football.
matchups.trashTalk: Silence of the CeeDee Lambs, you started a guy who scored zero for the second time in three weeks and still won by 12. Major Tuddy, your defense scored minus seven. Minus. Your defense didn't stop the other team, it scored for them. CeeDee Lamb had 20.2 and the Lambs still won. Even the name was laughing at you.

matchups.recap: Questionable or Kicked bounced back from last week's bench meltdown with 168.56, the second-best score of the week, and won by 38.36 with 0.0 left on the bench. Joe Burrow scored 33.16, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 31.1, and Isaiah Likely 27.7 at TE on a 12.21 projection. Stefon Diggs, last week's problem child, gave 20.3, Alvin Kamara 16.4 and Harold Fannin Jr. 16.1 at FLEX. Jason Myers kicked 2.0. Bang average got the comeback of the season from George Pickens: 0.0 last week, 43.5 this week, on a 12.25 projection, and that alone beat the margin. Nico Collins added 24.4. But Bryce Young gave 8.1 on an 18.8 projection, Tutu Atwell 4.1, and they played the whole game with an empty RB slot. Kenneth Walker III and Bucky Irving sat on the bench with 0.0 and Puka Nacua was on IR, so those three didn't cost a thing. But Corey Kiner scored 2.5 on the bench and could've filled that hole. You can't score from an empty chair.
matchups.trashTalk: Bang average, you started nine guys. The rule book says ten. Even your empty RB slot was bang average: zero points, zero effort, zero excuses. Questionable or Kicked, last week you lost it on your own bench, this week your bench was all zeros and you left nothing on it. Growth. Back in first, and it's a tie.

matchups.recap: The closest game of the week, by 11.42, and the first game for 1 season wonder (formerly Champ 🏆), who finally took the trophy off the sign. Honest. Painful, but honest. Deebo Samuel Sr. scored 25.9 on an 11.7 projection, Josh Allen 22.34 and Justin Jefferson 16.4. Then Kyren Williams gave 5.2 on an 18.63 projection, Jalen Coker 0.3, Tyler Warren 2.4 and Jakobi Meyers 6.4. And Quinshon Judkins, after two straight duds as a starter, got benched and scored 16.1. Put Judkins at RB for Kyren (+10.9), slide Deebo from RB/WR to WR in place of Coker, and move Kyren into RB/WR (+4.9 over Coker's 0.3). That's 127.14, which beats 122.76. Five straight losses, the last one gift-wrapped. AllIGoneToPot made it two straight wins behind Brock Purdy (31.66), Bijan Robinson (17.7), Ollie Gordon II (15.5) and DK Metcalf (15.4). Dak Prescott scored 34.42 on the bench, 2.76 more than Purdy. It's a one-QB league, so you pick one and live with it. They won anyway, so nobody's crying. Dominic Zvada kicked 2.0 and Travis Kelce gave 5.0.
matchups.trashTalk: 1 season wonder, I respect a team that reads its own scouting report. Last week the trophy emoji filed for divorce, this week it took the house. Five straight losses, alone in last, and you benched the one running back who showed up. AllIGoneToPot, two straight wins. Somebody check the sofa again, the stash is still paying out.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 21.76 and more than doubled it. The top starter in the league, in the highest-scoring game any team has posted all season. The highest Stud of the Week score of the season so far. False Hope finally made the name sound ironic.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: Projected for 23.86, one week after giving 13.4 on a 26.5 projection. Carried the whole Dream Team on his back while the quarterback scored 3.02. He did everything except win the game, and that wasn't his department.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 21.97, delivered 3.02. A shortfall of 18.95, the worst in the league. Honorable mentions: Kyren Williams (5.2 on 18.63), Brock Bowers (3.8 on 15.41) and Jalen Coker (0.3 on 11.26).

awards.label: Bench Blunder
awards.note: Quinshon Judkins scored 16.1 on the bench while Kyren Williams gave 5.2 at RB, a +10.9 swing. Then slide Deebo Samuel Sr. from RB/WR to WR in place of Jalen Coker (0.3) and move Kyren into RB/WR, another +4.9. That lineup scores 127.14, enough to beat AllIGoneToPot's 122.76. 15.8 points left on the bench in an 11.42-point loss. That's the fifth straight L, and this one was self-inflicted. Honorable mentions: Kelce's Wildest Dream Team sat Josh Downs (15.3) and Omarion Hampton (17.5) for 25.2 in legal swaps in a 45-point loss, and Bang average left an RB slot empty with Corey Kiner (2.5) on the bench.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.note: Projected for 5.46, delivered MINUS 7.0, the worst defensive score of the entire season, beating the Texans' -4.0 from Week 1. A 12.46-point shortfall in a 12.48-point loss for Major Tuddy. Even a projected afternoon still loses by 0.02, but nobody wants to hear that from me right now.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 12.25. Scored 0.0 last week and made my duds list. This week he scored 43.5 out of the FLEX, beat the projection by 31.25 and outscored the entire 38.36-point margin by himself. In a loss. Sorry, gang, that's the business.

momentOfWeek.text: Picture it, gang. You put a trophy right there in your team name, Champ 🏆, so every manager in this league has to look at it every Sunday. Then Week 10 rolls around. You're on a four-game losing streak, you scored 76.46 the week before, and somewhere in the dark of the night you open the settings and type it in yourself: 1 season wonder. No league vote. No intervention. Self-diagnosed. And then you go out and prove it. Quinshon Judkins, the guy you started for two straight weeks at 6.9 and 5.5, finally gets benched and scores 16.1. Kyren Williams, the guy you started instead, gives 5.2. Jalen Coker scores 0.3. You lose by 11.42 with 15.8 points sitting on the bench. Five straight losses. Alone in last at 3-7. Fewest points in the league. Coaches, I've seen a lot of rebrands in my day, but I've never seen one with a perfect first week like that. The name change wasn't a joke. It was a press release.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: Bounced back with 168.56, a perfect lineup and the league lead in points by 137.36 (1,517.66). Tied at the top but nobody's really tied with them.
Two straight wins and a share of first. Started Omar Cooper Jr. for another 0.0 and won anyway. Living dangerously and loving it.
Six-game streak snapped by a 190-point freight train. Still third in points (1,378.16), still allowing the most (1,428.04).
Season-high 190.58 and back to .500. CMC went for 46.3. The name is starting to look like false advertising.
Perfect lineup, lost by 12.48 because the defense scored minus seven. Two losses in three weeks. Blame the Steelers.
Mahomes 35.42, a perfect lineup and a 45-point win. Not done after all. Maybe just Medium Rare Dingos.
Pickens dropped 43.5 and they still lost by 38 with an empty RB slot. Fifth in points (1,351.3), four wins to show for it.
Two straight wins, out of last place, and no longer the fewest points in the league. The stash is holding up.
Gibbs 44.2, Maye 3.02, 25.2 points on the bench. Two straight losses. The dream is now a recurring nightmare.
Formerly Champ 🏆. Five straight losses, alone in last, fewest points in the league (1,199.44), and a bench blunder that cost the game. The name fits.

lastWord: That's Week 10, gang. A season high of 190.58 from a team called False Hope. A six-game streak dead on arrival. A defense that scored minus seven. A man who scored 0.0 last week scoring 43.5 this week. A team that started nine players. And a former champion who changed the name to match the results, then went out and lost with 16.1 on the bench. Two teams at 7-3, two at 6-4, one at 5-5, four at 4-6, and one at 3-7 wondering what happened to last year. Count your starters. Check your bench. And if you rename your team, make sure it's something you'd like to live up to. Reinebold out.
footerTagline: "Championships are forever. Team names are editable."
